## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. # the placeholder-echo failure that disqualified qwen - the literal string
  # "string" appearing in datasets/metrics. If either shows up, this model is
  # not usable for a hallucination-graded deliverable.
  #
  # qwen/qwen3.6-27b also has budget but stays REJECTED: T-004 measured it
  # echoing schema placeholders into datasets/metrics on 2 of 5 papers, which
  # silently injects fabricated content (SPEC 14.2 forbids exactly this).
  #
  # Restore 120b once its daily window refills, if the two runs are comparable.
  # ============================================================== TEMPORARY
  # 🔴 PAID PROVIDER, FOR 2026-08-28 ONLY. REVERT TOMORROW.
  #
  # This BREAKS TASKLIST 0.1 ("no paid models, no paid tiers, no trial
  # credits, at any point in this project"), knowingly and on the human's
  # explicit instruction, to unblock one T-409 test run after Groq's free tier
  # ran out of DAILY tokens on both gpt-oss models.
  #
  # What is preserved: the MODEL. Baseten serves the same open-weight
  # `openai/gpt-oss-120b` that the T-004 bake-off selected as PRIMARY, so this
  # run's output is comparable to a free-tier run rather than better than one.
  # Only the host is paid. Measured cost: ~4,730 tokens per extraction,
  # ~118,000 for 25 papers, roughly $0.02.
  #
  # The provider is stamped into outputs/runs/<id>/config.json and into every
  # cache entry, so no artefact produced this way can be reported as $0 by
  # accident.
  #
  # TOMORROW, REVERT TO:
  #     model: openai/gpt-oss-20b
  #     planner_model: openai/gpt-oss-20b
  #     provider: null
  #     requests_per_minute: 30
  #     tokens_per_minute: 8000
  #     review.max_papers: 10        <-- the human's instruction, see below
  # ==========================================================================
  model: openai/gpt-oss-120b       # T-004 PRIMARY. Same weights, paid host.
  planner_model: openai/gpt-oss-120b
  provider: baseten                # TEMPORARY - see the block above
  temperature: 0.1
  # 4096 -> 2048. Measured over 55 cached extractions: median response 571
  # tokens, p90 948, max 1,682. 4096 reserved 2.4x the largest response ever
  # produced, and that reservation is charged against TPM. Agents override:
  # extractor 2,048, writer 2,560 (prose sections need more than JSON).
  max_tokens: 2048
  # GROQ FREE-TIER LIMITS, verified live 2026-08-28 against
  # x-ratelimit-* headers and console.groq.com/docs/rate-limits.
  # Identical for openai/gpt-oss-120b, openai/gpt-oss-20b and qwen/qwen3.6-27b:
  #
  #     RPM     30          requests per minute
  #     RPD  1,000          requests per DAY
  #     TPM  8,000          tokens per minute   <-- THE ONE THAT BINDS
  #     TPD 200,000         tokens per day
  #
  # T-409 was refused constantly while holding 999 of 1,000 daily requests.
  # This project is token-bound, not request-bound, and the throttle used to
  # pace only requests - which is why lowering it 15 -> 4 changed nothing.
  #
  # Providers reserve `prompt + max_tokens` against the TPM bucket at
  # admission. With the old max_tokens 4096 and extractor prompts up to 18,000
  # chars (~4,500 tokens), the largest requests reserved ~8,600 tokens - more
  # than the entire bucket - so they could never be served at ANY rate. They
  # burned 5 retries x 60 s each and were written as blank insights.
  #
  # Now: llm.py estimates prompt+max_tokens, refuses an impossible request
  # immediately with TokenBudgetExceeded, and paces on a rolling 60 s token
  # ledger. requests_per_minute returns to Groq's real 30; tokens govern.
  # TEMPORARY (2026-08-28): Baseten is a paid endpoint with no 8,000 TPM free
  # cap, so the token pacing that Groq needs is switched off. Setting
  # tokens_per_minute to 0 also disables the TokenBudgetExceeded pre-flight,
  # which is correct here - that guard exists for a small free-tier bucket.
  # RESTORE 30 / 8000 when reverting to Groq, or the first free-tier run will
  # walk straight back into the 429 storm of 2026-08-28.
  requests_per_minute: 60

review:
  min_papers: 20
  # Lowered 60 -> 25 on 2026-08-28. Extraction is one sequential LLM call per
  # paper and the 6-example prompt made each slower, so 60 papers is ~60-90 min
  # against the ~30-minute tolerance in TASKLIST 0.2. 25 is also the size
  # TASKLIST already specifies for ablation runs (T-702/T-703), so the flagship
  # run and the ablations are now directly comparable rather than differently
  # sized.
  #
  # ⚠️ Consequence for T-409's recall figure: with a 35-paper answer key, the
  # CORPUS recall ceiling is 25/35 = 0.714. It cannot reach 0.80 at this
  # setting, by arithmetic, and must not be read as a retrieval failure.
  # UNION recall - did retrieval find the paper at all - is unaffected, and
  # decisions.txt D-04 already makes that the primary gate for exactly this
  # reason.
  # TEMPORARY 2026-08-28: 25 -> 10 for the end-to-end verification run on the
  # paid host. NOTE for the ablations: T-702/T-703 specify max_papers=25, so a
  # 10-paper run is NOT directly comparable to them. With a 35-paper answer key
  # this also caps CORPUS recall at 10/35 = 0.286 by arithmetic; UNION recall
  # (did retrieval find the paper at all) is unaffected and remains the gate
  # under decisions.txt D-04.
  max_papers: 10
  year_min: 2019
  max_iterations: 3                # hard cap, forced WRITE on the last
  grounding_threshold: 0.7
  coverage_threshold: 0.8

verifier:
  # CORRECTED 2026-08-28 (T-502). This named data/models/verifier-int8.onnx,

  # merely shares a name would score with a different vocabulary and degrade
  # silently rather than fail.

  support_threshold: 0.7           # biased to precision (T-503)

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\Sreekaran\.claude\plugins\cache\claude-plugins-official\superpowers\6.3.0\skills\systematic-debugging

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: ${IDENTITY:+SET}${IDENTITY:-UNSET}"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   env | grep IDENTITY || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?
   - Use the `superpowers:verification-before-completion` skill before claiming success

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

def search_openalex(
    query: str,
    *,
    year_min: int | None = None,
    max_results: int = 25,
    mailto: str = "sreekaran005@gmail.com",
    api_key: str | None = None,
) -> list[Paper]:
    """Search OpenAlex with ``title_and_abstract.search`` + date window.

    ``api_key`` defaults to ``OPENALEX_API_KEY`` from the environment. It is a
    **free registered key**, not a paid plan - verified 2026-08-27 that it
    reports ``prepaid-remaining-usd: 0``, so nothing is billable and TASKLIST
    §0.1 is satisfied. It raises the daily budget 10x:

        keyless   $0.10/day  ~  100 searches
        with key  $1.00/day  ~ 1000 searches

    Without it, evaluation work exhausts the day's quota in minutes.
    """
    key = api_key if api_key is not None else os.getenv("OPENALEX_API_KEY")
    filters = [f"title_and_abstract.search:{query}"]
    if year_min is not None:
        filters.append(f"from_publication_date:{year_min}-01-01")
        filters.append("to_publication_date:2026-12-31")
    filter_str = ",".join(filters)

    papers: list[Paper] = []
    cursor = "*"
    per_page = min(200, max_results)

    with httpx.Client(timeout=60.0, follow_redirects=True) as client:
        while len(papers) < max_results:
            params = {
                "filter": filter_str,
                "per-page": per_page,
                "cursor": cursor,
                # Courtesy only: measured 2026-08-27 that `mailto` no longer
                # buys any quota. The polite pool is gone.
                "mailto": mailto,
            }
            if key:
                params["api_key"] = key
            resp = client.get("https://api.openalex.org/works", params=params)
            if resp.status_code == 429:
                # ⚠️ OpenAlex moved to a METERED DAILY BUDGET (measured
                # 2026-08-27): x-ratelimit-limit-usd = $0.10/day, and a search
                # costs $0.001 -- roughly 100 searches per day. `mailto` no
                # longer buys extra budget; the polite pool is gone.
                #

def search_arxiv(query: str, *, max_results: int = 25) -> list[Paper]:
    """Search arXiv Atom API over HTTPS (HTTP returns empty 301 body)."""
    papers: list[Paper] = []
    start = 0
    page_size = min(50, max_results)

    with httpx.Client(timeout=60.0, follow_redirects=True) as client:
        while len(papers) < max_results:
            n = min(page_size, max_results - len(papers))
            params = {
                "search_query": f'all:"{query}"',
                "start": start,
                "max_results": n,
            }
            # Mandatory HTTPS — http:// returns 301 with empty body.
            #
            # 🔴 arXiv was the ONLY source without backoff, and it showed:
            # OpenAlex handles 429 explicitly and Semantic Scholar retries with
            # delay, but this was a bare raise_for_status(). arXiv asks for
            # <= 1 request / 3 s and throttles bursts, so three acceptance
            # tests calling search_arxiv back to back turned a throttle into a
            # test failure (2026-08-28: test_t203_dedup and test_t204_pdf both
            # died on httpx.HTTPStatusError while OpenAlex sat at 83% of its
            # daily budget — the wrong host got the blame).
            resp = _arxiv_get_with_backoff(client, params)

"""Offline reachability: can a query's AND-of-terms match a gold paper at all?

OpenAlex `title_and_abstract.search:<q>` is a stemmed AND over title+abstract.
A paper that does not contain EVERY term is excluded at the source - no
ranking, reranking or fusion can bring it back. This measures that ceiling
without spending a single API call.

Stemming is approximated (lowercase, strip plurals/-ing/-ed, prefix match on
stems >= 4 chars) and stopwords dropped, so counts are an UPPER bound on what
OpenAlex would match.
"""
import json, re, sys, pathlib

SCRATCH = pathlib.Path(sys.argv[1])
gold = json.load(open(SCRATCH / "gold_text.json", encoding="utf-8"))
docs = {v["doi"]: (v["title"] + " " + v["abstract"]).lower() for v in gold.values()}

STOP = {"a", "an", "the", "of", "in", "on", "for", "and", "or", "to", "with", "via"}


def stem(w: str) -> str:
    for suf in ("ations", "ation", "ing", "ies", "ed", "es", "s"):
        if len(w) - len(suf) >= 4 and w.endswith(suf):
            return w[: -len(suf)]
    return w


def terms(q: str) -> list[str]:
    return [stem(w) for w in re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", q.lower()) if w not in STOP]


def matches(q: str, doc: str) -> bool:
    words = {stem(w) for w in re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", doc)}
    return all(any(w.startswith(t) for w in words) for t in terms(q))


def reach(q: str) -> list[str]:
    return [doi for doi, doc in docs.items() if matches(q, doc)]

content.text:
Root cause found and measured. No fix applied yet — the fix has a cost you should choose.

## The Planner's queries can't reach the gold papers at all

OpenAlex is queried with `filter=title_and_abstract.search:<query>` (`search_sources.py:134`), which **ANDs every term**. A paper missing any one term is excluded at the source — no reranker, fusion or cap change can bring it back.

I measured that ceiling offline against the 34 gold papers' real title+abstract text:

| query set | gold papers the AND filter can reach |
|---|---|
| the flagship's 12 Planner queries | **3 / 34** |
| the 15 hand-written stand-ins | **27 / 34** |

Observed union recall was 2/35. **The run was already at its ceiling.** Nothing downstream was underperforming — the papers were never retrievable.

## It is not vocabulary, and not query length — it is conjunction width

Both sets average ~3.6 terms, so length alone isn't the discriminator. But when I keep only the best 2-term subset **of each Planner query's own words**, reachability goes 3 → 25 of 34. The information was there; the third and fourth term threw it away. The pattern is consistent: the surviving pair is the anchor (`retrieval`, `hallucination`, `citation`, `prompt`), and what kills the query is the descriptor the Planner adds to express the sub-question — `architecture`, `selection`, `integration`, `domains`, `assessment`, `design`, `summary`. Those words describe the research need; they don't appear in the literature's own text.

This also confirms the T-409 note (`TASKLIST.md:368`) — *"do not spend on `bge-base`, query shape dominates"* — with evidence rather than assertion. **The Aug 28 kill switch's prescribed fix (`bge-small` → `bge-base`) would have changed nothing.** 12 of the 13 gold hits in the 0.371 pool came from OpenAlex, which both runs had enabled, so it isn't source composition either.

## Measured live against today's index

Same 12 Planner queries, same connector, one variable — the expansion policy:

| policy | searches | pool | union recall |
|---|---|---|---|
| as issued (flagship) | 12 | 288 | **0.057** (2/35) — reproduces exactly |
| + every 2-term subset | 72 | 1,517 | **0.229** (8/35) |
| + every 2-term subset, cap 100/query | 72 | 5,857 | **0.400** (14/35) |

The cap matters because 6 of the 14 gold papers were found *below rank 25* (at 27, 29, 31, 37, 61, 88). Cost of the last row: ~7% of the daily OpenAlex budget and ~3 minutes of retrieval.

**0.400 from generated queries beats the 0.371 hand-written baseline.** It is still not 0.80 — but the gate isn't index-bound: of the 21 gold papers still unfound, **17 of 18 testable ones come back at rank 1–2 when searched by their own title**. They're in OpenAlex and matchable; the queries just never ask for them.

## Two defects worth fixing regardless

**A comma or question mark in a query returns HTTP 400.** Both are filter-syntax metacharacters and neither is escaped. Confirmed by isolation — `,` and `?` fail, while `:`, `|`, apostrophes and unicode hyphens are fine. It killed 3 of my 21 title probes. The main path survives today only because the Planner happens to emit bare keywords and has no raw-question fallback; nothing prevents it emitting a comma.

**`MAX_QUERY_TERMS = 6`, and the validator tells the model to write "3-5 **specific** terms"** (`planner.py:57`, `:140-145`). The comment there already knows OpenAlex ANDs terms — the constant is just calibrated wrong, and "specific" is precisely the instruction that causes the failure. At 3–5 terms reachability is 3/34.

## What I'd do

Fix the 400 bug (small, independent, testable), then recalibrate the Planner to emit 2-term anchor queries and issue the pair-expansions, keeping `max_per_source` at 25 → ~0.23, pool ~1,500, no downstream cost change. Raising the cap to 100 is what gets 0.400, but it puts 5,857 papers into embedding and ranking, and T-212 rejected `max_per_source: 100` once before for hurting the top-60 gate — that one deserves its own measurement rather than a config edit.

Which do you want: the bug fix alone, the bug fix plus the query policy at cap 25, or the full 0.400 configuration with the downstream cost measured first? The probe scripts and their JSON are in the scratchpad — say the word and I'll fold them into `eval/` as a permanent harness and record the finding against T-409.

def estimate_tokens(text: str) -> int:
    """Approximate token count. Deliberately crude and deliberately high.

    Four characters per token is the usual English rule of thumb. We do not
    tokenize for real because the budget check only has to be *conservative* -
    over-estimating costs a little throughput, under-estimating costs a 429
    storm, so the error is priced asymmetrically and we round up.
    """
    return len(text) // 4 + 1


class LLMError(RuntimeError):

content.text:
Short answer: **`max_per_source` costs you no LLM tokens at all.** It never reaches the model. The thing it does cost is CPU, and that's where cap 100 breaks.

## Why quota isn't the constraint

`max_per_source` appears in exactly one file — `retriever.py:160,195`. Nothing downstream reads it. Only three agents call the LLM (planner, extractor, writer), and each is driven by `max_papers`: the extractor takes `papers[:max_papers]` (`extractor.py:272`), the writer the same (`writer.py:178`). A bigger pool changes *which* 10 papers get extracted, never *how many*.

Measured from the flagship run's own 14 cached prompts:

| | |
|---|---|
| requests | 14 (1 planner + 10 extractor + 3 writer) |
| actual tokens | 60,173 |
| **reserved** (prompt + `max_tokens`) | **79,599** |

Reserved is the right unit — your 429 body said `Requested 5520`, which is exactly a 3,472-token prompt plus `max_tokens: 2048`. Groq charges the reservation at admission.

Against Groq's free tier at `max_papers: 10`:

- **TPD 200,000 per model → ~2.5 runs/day.** Unchanged whether `max_per_source` is 25 or 100.
- **TPM 8,000** — largest single request reserves 6,538, so it's admissible, but it paces to ~1.2 requests/min: roughly 12 minutes of pure waiting per run.
- 20b and 120b hold **separate** 200k buckets, so you have ~5 runs/day across both. Baseten isn't needed for this — the LLM load doesn't move.

One real cost: changing `max_per_source` changes the top-10, so every extraction prompt is a cache miss. Each new retrieval configuration costs one fresh run's ~80k tokens. That's 2 configurations per day per model, not 2 total.

## Where cap 100 actually breaks: the ranker

`ranker.py:153-170` deliberately widens the first stage to the whole corpus (`dense_k = sparse_k = len(chunks)`) and reranks **every candidate, once per sub-question**. So it's linear in pool size × 6.

Measured on your machine just now: **16 chunks/s** embedding, **31 pairs/s** reranking (33 ms each). Against the flagship's 640 chunks that predicts ~164s versus the 212.6s actually observed — same order, so the rates are sound. Projecting:

| config | pool | chunks | embed | rerank | **run total** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| flagship (today) | 271 | 640 | 40s | 124s | **5.3 min** (measured) |
| P3 @ cap 25 | 1,517 | ~3,600 | ~4 min | ~12 min | **~19 min** |
| P3 @ cap 100 | 5,857 | ~13,800 | ~14 min | ~45 min | **~63 min** |

Your tolerance is ~30 min (`TASKLIST §0.2`). Cap 25 fits; cap 100 is roughly double, and that's before the loop ever fires a second iteration.

So the constraint on `max_per_source: 100` was never the quota — it's that the ranker cross-encodes the entire corpus six times. Which also means the 0.400 result isn't out of reach: bounding the rerank stage (fuse dense+sparse to a top-N, say 300, then cross-encode only those) takes that 45 minutes to about 1 minute and keeps the wider pool. The comment at `ranker.py:153` says the widening was deliberate — the old global top-60 was silently discarding papers — so that's a change to make deliberately and measure, not a config edit.

Want me to measure the bounded-rerank variant against the gold set? It's local-only, costs no tokens and no API budget, and it's the thing that decides whether 0.400 is affordable.

"""T-403 — the Retriever node. Wraps Phase 2; makes no LLM call.

`SPEC §7.2`. Executes the Planner's ``search_plan`` across the enabled
connectors, deduplicates, chunks, and returns **only what is new**.

⚠️ **Deduplication is this node's job, and nothing else will do it.**
``graph/state.py`` gives ``papers`` and ``chunks`` an ``add`` reducer so that a
Critic RETRIEVE loop *adds* coverage instead of starting over. The cost of that
choice is that a retriever which returns a paper already in state duplicates it
silently, and the corpus quietly inflates on iteration 2. ``agents/base.py``
enforces the contract, but the actual identity logic lives here because only
this node knows that the same paper arrives from three sources under three ids.

**Dedup key, in priority order** (T-203):

1. **normalised DOI** — the only real identifier. ``normalise_doi`` already
   strips the ``https://doi.org/`` prefix and lowercases.
2. **normalised title** — for the roughly 1-in-5 OpenAlex records with no DOI,
   and to bridge an arXiv preprint to its published version, which carry
   *different* DOIs (``10.48550/arxiv.*`` vs the publisher's) but the same
   title. Requires ≥25 alphanumeric characters so that short or truncated
   titles cannot collide.

When two records collide, the **richer** one wins: a version with an abstract
beats one without, because T-204/T-505 gate claim-sourcing on
``text_availability`` and an abstract-less duplicate would silently downgrade a
paper the pipeline could otherwise use.

**Degradation is per-source and per-query.** One connector failing, or the
OpenAlex daily budget expiring mid-plan (§0.2 — it is metered now), must not
lose the papers already gathered. Every failure is recorded in
``retrieval_log`` so a thin corpus is diagnosable after the fact rather than by
re-running a 30-minute pipeline.
"""

"""T-410 acceptance — query widening, and the cap that was never applied.

Offline. These test the *mechanism* that T-409's recall failure exposed; the
recall number itself is measured by a live run (``eval/flagship_recall.py``).

WHY THIS EXISTS (measured 2026-08-29, against the 34 gold papers whose
title+abstract OpenAlex actually holds):

    query set                                   gold papers the AND filter
                                                can reach, at ANY cap
    the flagship's 12 Planner queries                    3 / 34
    the same 12, plus every 2-term subset               31 / 34

``filter=title_and_abstract.search:<q>`` ANDs every term, so a paper missing
one term is excluded at the source - before ranking, fusion or the per-query
cap can see it. The flagship run scored union recall 2/35 against a ceiling of
3/34: it was not underperforming, it was *at* its ceiling. Widening the query
is therefore the only change that can raise the ceiling, and raising the cap is
the only change that can then collect what the wider query reaches. Neither
works alone, which is what these tests pin.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
from unittest.mock import patch

import pytest

from researchgpt.agents.planner import Planner
from researchgpt.agents.retriever import Retriever, expand_query
from researchgpt.core.config import load_config
from researchgpt.core.models import Paper, SearchTask

REPO = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def cfg():
    return load_config(str(REPO / "configs" / "default.yaml"))


def make_paper(pid):
    return Paper(
        paper_id=pid, doi=f"10.1/{pid}",
        title=f"A sufficiently long distinctive title number {pid}",
        source="openalex", abstract="An abstract. " * 30,
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# expand_query — the widening itself
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_t410_expansion_leads_with_the_original_query():
    """The Planner's own query is still asked first. Widening ADDS reach; it
    must never replace the specific query the plan asked for."""
    out = expand_query("prompt design retrieval agents")
    assert out[0] == "prompt design retrieval agents"


def test_t410_expansion_emits_every_two_term_subset():
    """Measured: the best-reaching pair is not predictable from position. For
    'multi agent retrieval architecture' it is 'multi retrieval'; for
    'benchmark dataset literature review' it is 'benchmark dataset'. A
    head-pair heuristic reaches 25/34, all pairs reach 31/34, so we issue all
    of them."""
    out = expand_query("prompt design retrieval agents")
    pairs = set(out[1:])
    assert pairs == {
        "prompt design", "prompt retrieval", "prompt agents",
        "design retrieval", "design agents", "retrieval agents",
    }


def test_t410_expansion_drops_stopwords_before_pairing():
    """'hallucination in scientific summarization' is 4 tokens but 3 TERMS.
    Pairing on the raw tokens would spend searches on 'hallucination in'."""
    out = expand_query("hallucination in scientific summarization")
    assert all(" in" not in q and "in " not in q for q in out[1:])
    assert set(out[1:]) == {
        "hallucination scientific", "hallucination summarization",
        "scientific summarization",
    }


def test_t410_a_two_term_query_expands_to_itself_alone():
    """Its only pair IS itself. Issuing it twice would pay for the same search
    twice against a metered daily budget."""
    assert expand_query("RAG survey") == ["RAG survey"]


def test_t410_expansion_is_deduplicated_and_order_stable():
    """The retrieval log and the trace are read by a human comparing runs."""
    q = "retrieval augmented retrieval review"
    out = expand_query(q)
    assert len(out) == len(set(out)), out
    assert out == expand_query(q)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The cap that was never applied
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_t410_planner_does_not_pin_the_per_query_cap(cfg):
    """🔴 REGRESSION. The retriever caps at ``min(task.max_results,
    max_per_source)`` and the Planner used to hardcode ``max_results or 25`` -
    a value its own prompt puts in every few-shot example. Raising
    ``max_per_source`` to 100 in the config was therefore a NO-OP: min(25, 100)
    is 25. The retrieval budget is an operator decision, not a model one, so
    the model's number is ignored and the field is left unset."""
    payload = {
        "sub_questions": [{"id": "SQ1", "text": "What is X?", "facet": "method"}],
        "search_plan": [{"sq_id": "SQ1", "query": "retrieval augmented generation",
                         "sources": ["openalex"], "max_results": 25}],
        "assumptions": [],
    }
    _, plan, _ = Planner._validate(payload)
    assert plan[0].max_results is None, (
        "the model's max_results must not become the cap; leave it unset so "
        "sources.max_per_source governs"
    )


def test_t410_retriever_asks_every_source_for_the_configured_cap(cfg):
    """The end of the same regression: with the field unset, the retriever must
    ask for the operator's ``max_per_source``, not 25."""
    seen: list[tuple[str, int]] = []

    def spy(self, source, query, year_min, limit):
        seen.append((query, limit))
        return [make_paper(f"{query}-{limit}")]

    with patch.object(Retriever, "_search", spy):
        Retriever(cfg)({"iteration": 0, "papers": [],
                        "search_plan": [SearchTask(sq_id="SQ1", query="a b",
                                                   sources=["openalex"])]})
    assert seen, "no search was issued"
    assert {limit for _, limit in seen} == {cfg.sources.max_per_source}


def test_t410_retriever_issues_the_widened_queries(cfg):
    """One 4-term task becomes 7 searches: the original plus 6 pairs."""
    seen: list[str] = []

    def spy(self, source, query, year_min, limit):
        seen.append(query)
        return [make_paper(query)]

    with patch.object(Retriever, "_search", spy):
        out = Retriever(cfg)({"iteration": 0, "papers": [],
                              "search_plan": [
                                  SearchTask(sq_id="SQ1",
                                             query="prompt design retrieval agents",
                                             sources=["openalex"])]})
    assert seen == expand_query("prompt design retrieval agents")
    assert len(out["papers"]) == 7


def test_t410_the_widened_queries_are_traceable_to_their_parent(cfg):
    """A run is diagnosed from ``retrieval_log`` months later. A log that says
    only 'prompt retrieval' loses which planned task asked for it - and every
    comparison of a widened run against the flagship needs that link."""
    with patch.object(Retriever, "_search",
                      lambda self, s, q, y, limit: [make_paper(q)]):
        out = Retriever(cfg)({"iteration": 0, "papers": [],
                              "search_plan": [
                                  SearchTask(sq_id="SQ1",
                                             query="prompt design retrieval agents",
                                             sources=["openalex"])]})
    log = out["retrieval_log"]
    assert {row["query"] for row in log} == set(expand_query("prompt design retrieval agents"))
    assert {row["planned_query"] for row in log} == {"prompt design retrieval agents"}
    assert {row["sq_id"] for row in log} == {"SQ1"}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The connector bug the investigation turned up
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_t410_openalex_query_escapes_filter_metacharacters():
    """🔴 A comma or a question mark in a query returns HTTP 400 from OpenAlex:
    both are filter-syntax metacharacters (`,` separates filters, `?` ends the
    query string) and neither was escaped. Measured 2026-08-29 - it killed 3 of
    21 title probes. `:`, `|`, apostrophes and unicode hyphens are all fine.

    The main path survives today only because the Planner happens to emit bare
    keywords; nothing stops an LLM emitting a comma."""
    from researchgpt.tools.search_sources import sanitise_openalex_query as clean

    assert "," not in clean("natural language processing, machine learning")
    assert "?" not in clean("can large language models replace humans?")
    # Legitimate characters survive: stripping them would change the query.
    assert clean("hallucination: a survey") == "hallucination: a survey"
    assert clean("gpt-4's efficacy") == "gpt-4's efficacy"

"""T-410 acceptance — query widening, and the cap that was never applied.

Offline. These test the *mechanism* that T-409's recall failure exposed; the
recall number itself is measured by a live run (``eval/flagship_recall.py``).

WHY THIS EXISTS (measured 2026-08-29, against the 34 gold papers whose
title+abstract OpenAlex actually holds):

    query set                                   gold papers the AND filter
                                                can reach, at ANY cap
    the flagship's 12 Planner queries                    3 / 34
    the same 12, plus every 2-term subset               31 / 34

``filter=title_and_abstract.search:<q>`` ANDs every term, so a paper missing
one term is excluded at the source - before ranking, fusion or the per-query
cap can see it. The flagship run scored union recall 2/35 against a ceiling of
3/34: it was not underperforming, it was *at* its ceiling. Widening the query
is therefore the only change that can raise the ceiling, and raising the cap is
the only change that can then collect what the wider query reaches. Neither
works alone, which is what these tests pin.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import pathlib
from unittest.mock import patch

import pytest

from researchgpt.agents.planner import Planner
from researchgpt.agents.retriever import Retriever, expand_query
from researchgpt.core.config import load_config
from researchgpt.core.models import Paper, SearchTask

REPO = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def cfg():
    return load_config(str(REPO / "configs" / "default.yaml"))


def make_paper(pid):
    return Paper(
        paper_id=pid, doi=f"10.1/{pid}",
        title=f"A sufficiently long distinctive title number {pid}",
        source="openalex", abstract="An abstract. " * 30,
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# expand_query — the widening itself
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_t410_expansion_leads_with_the_original_query():
    """The Planner's own query is still asked first. Widening ADDS reach; it
    must never replace the specific query the plan asked for."""
    out = expand_query("prompt design retrieval agents")
    assert out[0] == "prompt design retrieval agents"


def test_t410_expansion_emits_every_two_term_subset():
    """Measured: the best-reaching pair is not predictable from position. For
    'multi agent retrieval architecture' it is 'multi retrieval'; for
    'benchmark dataset literature review' it is 'benchmark dataset'. A
    head-pair heuristic reaches 25/34, all pairs reach 31/34, so we issue all
    of them."""
    out = expand_query("prompt design retrieval agents")
    pairs = set(out[1:])
    assert pairs == {
        "prompt design", "prompt retrieval", "prompt agents",
        "design retrieval", "design agents", "retrieval agents",
    }


def test_t410_expansion_drops_stopwords_before_pairing():
    """'hallucination in scientific summarization' is 4 tokens but 3 TERMS.
    Pairing on the raw tokens would spend searches on 'hallucination in'."""
    out = expand_query("hallucination in scientific summarization")
    assert all(" in" not in q and "in " not in q for q in out[1:])
    assert set(out[1:]) == {
        "hallucination scientific", "hallucination summarization",
        "scientific summarization",
    }


def test_t410_a_two_term_query_expands_to_itself_alone():
    """Its only pair IS itself. Issuing it twice would pay for the same search
    twice against a metered daily budget."""
    assert expand_query("RAG survey") == ["RAG survey"]


def test_t410_expansion_is_deduplicated_and_order_stable():
    """The retrieval log and the trace are read by a human comparing runs."""
    q = "retrieval augmented retrieval review"

"""T-409 / T-213(1) — score a real pipeline run against the answer key.

TASKLIST T-409 runs the system on **its own topic**, where the project's
hand-curated 35-paper bibliography is the answer key. That makes the flagship
run do double duty, and the second job has been blocked since Phase 2:

> **T-212**: *"Re-run this gate right after T-402 and treat that as the real
> Phase 2 gate."*

The original gate read **union recall 0.371 / Recall@60 0.057** using 15
hand-written stand-in queries, and T-213's diagnosis was that the misses were
*never asked for* rather than unreachable. The Planner (T-402) is the fix. This
module measures whether it worked, on the queries the Planner actually emitted
rather than on a stand-in.

**Two numbers, and they answer different questions** (`decisions.txt` D-04):

* **union recall** — of the 35 gold papers, how many did retrieval find *at
  all*? This is a hard ceiling: no reranker can promote a paper that was never
  fetched. **This is the primary gate.**
* **Recall@N** — how many survived into the ``max_papers`` corpus the Extractor
  actually read? Bounded by ``max_papers / 35`` and by how the round-robin
  splits slots across sub-questions, so it is reported, not gated.

Matching is DOI-first with a title fallback, the same rule the T-212 harness
uses, so the numbers are comparable to the 2026-08-26 baseline.

Run::

    python -m researchgpt.eval.flagship_recall --run flagship
"""

import json
import pathlib
import re
from typing import Any

DEFAULT_OUT = pathlib.Path("eval/flagship_recall_t409.json")

#: Same floor as the retriever's dedup key: shorter titles are not distinctive.

def norm_title(title: str | None) -> str:
    key = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "", (title or "").lower())
    return key if len(key) >= MIN_TITLE_KEY else ""

"""Returns (doi -> paper, title_key -> doi)."""
    doc = json.loads(GOLD.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    by_doi, by_title = {}, {}
    for paper in doc["papers"]:
        doi = norm_doi(paper.get("doi"))
        if doi:
            by_doi[doi] = paper
        title = norm_title(paper.get("title"))
        if title and doi:
            by_title[title] = doi
    return by_doi, by_title


def match(record: dict[str, Any], by_doi: dict, by_title: dict) -> str | None:
    """The gold DOI this record corresponds to, or None."""
    doi = norm_doi(record.get("doi"))
    if doi and doi in by_doi:
        return doi
    title = norm_title(record.get("title"))
    if title and title in by_title:
        return by_title[title]
    return None


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="T-409 - score a run against the answer key.")
    ap.add_argument("--run", default="flagship")
    ap.add_argument("--runs-dir", type=pathlib.Path, default=pathlib.Path("outputs/runs"))
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=pathlib.Path, default=DEFAULT_OUT)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    run_dir = args.runs_dir / args.run
    corpus_path = run_dir / "corpus.json"
    if not corpus_path.exists():
        raise SystemExit(
            f"{corpus_path} missing. The run must persist its corpus - see "
            f"write_corpus() in output/writers.py."
        )
    corpus = json.loads(corpus_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    retrieved = corpus["papers"]
    extracted_ids = set(corpus.get("extracted_paper_ids") or [])

    by_doi, by_title = load_gold()
    n_gold = len(by_doi)

    found_union: dict[str, dict] = {}
    found_corpus: dict[str, dict] = {}
    for record in retrieved:
        gold_doi = match(record, by_doi, by_title)
        if not gold_doi:
            continue
        found_union.setdefault(gold_doi, record)
        if record.get("paper_id") in extracted_ids:
            found_corpus.setdefault(gold_doi, record)

    union_recall = len(found_union) / n_gold
    corpus_recall = len(found_corpus) / n_gold
    missed = sorted(set(by_doi) - set(found_union))

    print("T-409 / T-213(1) - recall against the answer key\n")
    print(f"  run                  {args.run}")
    print(f"  gold papers          {n_gold}")
    print(f"  papers retrieved     {len(retrieved)}")
    print(f"  corpus extracted     {len(extracted_ids)}")
    print()
    print(f"  UNION RECALL         {len(found_union):3d}/{n_gold}   {union_recall:.3f}"
          f"   <- the primary gate (D-04)")
    print(f"  corpus recall        {len(found_corpus):3d}/{n_gold}   {corpus_recall:.3f}"

    print()
    print("  2026-08-26 baseline, 15 stand-in queries:  union 0.371")
    delta = union_recall - 0.371
    print(f"  DELTA from the Planner (T-402):            {delta:+.3f}")
    print()

        print(f"  still missed ({len(missed)}):")
        for doi in missed[:10]:
            print(f"    {by_doi[doi]['title'][:66]}")

    args.out.write_text(json.dumps({

        "found": sorted(found_union),
        "missed": missed,

"""T-410 — every metric a completed run can be scored on, in one report.

``flagship_recall.py`` answers one question (did retrieval find the gold
papers at all). This answers the rest, from the same two files every run
already writes — ``corpus.json`` and ``trace.jsonl`` — so it can be pointed at
any past run and produce a comparable row. Nothing here re-runs the pipeline
and nothing here calls a model.

**On precision.** Two different precisions get called by that name here and
they are NOT interchangeable:

* **retrieval precision@k** — of the top *k* ranked papers, how many are in
  the answer key. With a 35-paper key against a pool in the thousands this is
  necessarily tiny, and it is *not* a quality verdict: a paper absent from one
  researcher's bibliography is not thereby irrelevant. Report it as ranking
  behaviour, never as "the system is 3% accurate".
* **grounding precision** — of the claims the Writer made, how many the
  Verifier could support against the cited paper. This one *is* a quality
  measure, and it is the one `SPEC §14.2` cares about.

**Ranking order.** ``corpus.json`` lists papers in the order the Ranker left
them (``agents/ranker.py`` reorders ``state['papers']`` in place), so index
position IS rank. If that ever stops being true, every @k number here silently
becomes insertion order — the defect that made the T-212 harness read 0.029
instead of 0.057 — so the report prints the check rather than assuming it.

Run::

    python -m researchgpt.eval.run_metrics --run t410_cap100
    python -m researchgpt.eval.run_metrics --run flagship --compare t410_cap100
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import collections
import json
import pathlib
from datetime import datetime
from typing import Any

from researchgpt.eval.flagship_recall import load_gold, match

AT_K = (10, 20, 40, 60, 100, 250, 500)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# loading
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def load_run(run_dir: pathlib.Path) -> tuple[dict, list[dict]]:
    corpus_path = run_dir / "corpus.json"
    trace_path = run_dir / "trace.jsonl"
    if not corpus_path.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"{corpus_path} missing - did the run finish?")
    corpus = json.loads(corpus_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    rows = []
    if trace_path.exists():
        for line in trace_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
            try:
                rows.append(json.loads(line))
            except Exception:
                pass
    return corpus, rows


def last_payload(rows: list[dict], event: str) -> dict:
    for row in reversed(rows):
        if row.get("event") == event:
            return row.get("payload") or {}
    return {}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# metrics
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def retrieval_metrics(corpus: dict) -> dict[str, Any]:
    by_doi, by_title = load_gold()
    n_gold = len(by_doi)
    papers = corpus["papers"]
    extracted = set(corpus.get("extracted_paper_ids") or [])

    # rank position (1-indexed) of every gold paper, first occurrence wins
    ranks: dict[str, int] = {}
    in_corpus: set[str] = set()
    for i, record in enumerate(papers, 1):
        gold_doi = match(record, by_doi, by_title)
        if not gold_doi:
            continue
        ranks.setdefault(gold_doi, i)
        if record.get("paper_id") in extracted:
            in_corpus.add(gold_doi)

    at_k = {}
    for k in AT_K:
        if k > len(papers):
            continue
        hits = sum(1 for r in ranks.values() if r <= k)
        at_k[k] = {"hits": hits, "recall": hits / n_gold, "precision": hits / k}

    mrr = sum(1 / r for r in ranks.values()) / n_gold if ranks else 0.0
    return {
        "gold_papers": n_gold,
        "pool_size": len(papers),
        "corpus_size": len(extracted),
        "union_recall": len(ranks) / n_gold,
        "corpus_recall": len(in_corpus) / n_gold,
        "mrr": mrr,
        "best_rank": min(ranks.values()) if ranks else None,
        "median_rank": sorted(ranks.values())[len(ranks) // 2] if ranks else None,
        "at_k": at_k,
        "gold_ranks": dict(sorted(ranks.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])),
        "missed": sorted(set(by_doi) - set(ranks)),
    }


def source_metrics(corpus: dict, rows: list[dict]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    log = corpus.get("retrieval_log") or []
    by_source = collections.Counter()
    returned = collections.Counter()
    errors = collections.Counter()
    for entry in log:
        by_source[entry["source"]] += entry.get("new") or 0
        returned[entry["source"]] += entry.get("returned") or 0
        if entry.get("error"):
            errors[entry["source"]] += 1
    planned = {e.get("planned_query", e.get("query")) for e in log}
    issued = {e["query"] for e in log}
    return {
        "planned_queries": len(planned),
        "issued_queries": len(issued),
        "widening_factor": round(len(issued) / len(planned), 2) if planned else None,
        "source_queries": len(log),
        "new_papers_by_source": dict(by_source),
        "returned_by_source": dict(returned),
        "errors_by_source": dict(errors),
        "papers_by_source": dict(collections.Counter(
            p.get("source") for p in corpus["papers"])),
    }


def quality_metrics(rows: list[dict]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    extract = last_payload(rows, "extract_summary")
    verify = last_payload(rows, "verification_summary")
    review = last_payload(rows, "review_written")
    decisions = [r["payload"].get("decision") for r in rows
                 if r.get("event") == "critic_decision"]
    claims = verify.get("claims") or 0
    supported = verify.get("supported") or 0
    partial = verify.get("partial") or 0
    dropped = verify.get("dropped") or 0
    return {
        "extraction": {
            "papers": extract.get("papers"),
            "mean_fields_of_8": extract.get("mean_fields_of_8"),
            "repair_passes": extract.get("repair_passes"),
            "failed_after_repairs": extract.get("failed_after_repairs"),
            "placeholder_echoes_removed": extract.get("placeholder_echoes_removed"),
            "skipped_no_text": extract.get("skipped_no_text"),
        },
        "writing": {
            "sections": review.get("sections"),
            "references": review.get("references"),
            "chars": review.get("chars"),
            "citations_dropped": review.get("citations_dropped"),
        },
        "verification": {
            "claims": claims,
            "supported": supported,
            "partial": partial,
            "unsupported_dropped": dropped,
            "contradicted": verify.get("contradicted"),
            "abstract_only_capped": verify.get("abstract_only_capped"),
            "grounding_score": verify.get("grounding_score"),
            # The headline quality number: of the claims written, the share the
            # Verifier could stand behind at all (SUPPORTED or PARTIAL).
            "grounding_precision": (claims - dropped) / claims if claims else None,
            # And the strict one: full support, not partial.
            "strict_precision": supported / claims if claims else None,
        },
        "loop": {
            "critic_decisions": decisions,
            "iterations": max((r.get("iteration") or 0) for r in rows) if rows else 0,
            "replans": sum(1 for d in decisions if d == "REPLAN"),
        },
    }


def cost_metrics(rows: list[dict], cache_dir: pathlib.Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    from researchgpt.core.llm import estimate_tokens

    requests = [r for r in rows if r.get("event") == "request"]
    prompt_tokens = response_tokens = 0
    for req in requests:
        digest = (req.get("payload") or {}).get("prompt_hash")
        path = cache_dir / f"{digest}.json"
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        entry = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        prompt_tokens += estimate_tokens(entry.get("prompt") or "")
        response_tokens += estimate_tokens(entry.get("response") or "")

    per_agent: dict[str, float] = {}
    started: dict[str, datetime] = {}
    for row in rows:
        when = datetime.fromisoformat(row["ts"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if row.get("event") == "agent_start":
            started[row["agent"]] = when
        elif row.get("event") == "agent_end" and row["agent"] in started:
            per_agent[row["agent"]] = round(
                per_agent.get(row["agent"], 0.0)
                + (when - started[row["agent"]]).total_seconds(), 1)
    wall = 0.0
    if rows:
        wall = (datetime.fromisoformat(rows[-1]["ts"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
                - datetime.fromisoformat(rows[0]["ts"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
                ).total_seconds()
    return {
        "llm_requests": len(requests),
        "prompt_tokens_est": prompt_tokens,
        "response_tokens_est": response_tokens,
        "total_tokens_est": prompt_tokens + response_tokens,
        # What the provider actually reserves per request at admission, which is
        # the number that exhausts a daily budget (measured from a Groq 429:
        # "Requested 5520" = a 3,472-token prompt + max_tokens 2048).
        "reserved_tokens_est": prompt_tokens + 2048 * len(requests),
        "wall_seconds": round(wall, 1),
        "seconds_by_agent": per_agent,
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# report
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def collect(run: str, runs_dir: pathlib.Path, cache_dir: pathlib.Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    corpus, rows = load_run(runs_dir / run)
    return {
        "run": run,
        "retrieval": retrieval_metrics(corpus),
        "sources": source_metrics(corpus, rows),
        "quality": quality_metrics(rows),
        "cost": cost_metrics(rows, cache_dir),
        "ranking_order_verified": bool(
            last_payload(rows, "rank_summary")), # a rank_summary means the
        # Ranker ran; without it corpus.json is insertion order and every @k
        # below is meaningless (the T-212 defect).
    }


def render(m: dict[str, Any], base: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> None:
    r, s, q, c = m["retrieval"], m["sources"], m["quality"], m["cost"]

    def delta(new, old, fmt="{:+.3f}"):
        if base is None or old is None or new is None:
            return ""
        return "   " + fmt.format(new - old)

    br = base["retrieval"] if base else None
    print(f"\n{'=' * 74}\nRUN METRICS - {m['run']}\n{'=' * 74}")
    if base:
        print(f"(deltas against {base['run']})")
    if not m["ranking_order_verified"]:
        print("\n  !! no rank_summary in the trace - corpus.json is INSERTION "
              "order, so every @k number below is meaningless")

    print(f"\n-- retrieval, against a {r['gold_papers']}-paper answer key "
          f"{'-' * 22}")
    print(f"  pool size            {r['pool_size']:6d}"
          + (f"   ({base['retrieval']['pool_size']} before)" if base else ""))
    print(f"  UNION RECALL         {r['union_recall']:6.3f}   "
          f"({len(r['gold_ranks'])}/{r['gold_papers']})"
          + delta(r["union_recall"], br and br["union_recall"]))
    print(f"  corpus recall        {r['corpus_recall']:6.3f}   "
          f"(bounded by max_papers/{r['gold_papers']})"
          + delta(r["corpus_recall"], br and br["corpus_recall"]))
    print(f"  MRR                  {r['mrr']:6.3f}"
          + delta(r["mrr"], br and br["mrr"]))
    print(f"  best / median rank   {r['best_rank']} / {r['median_rank']}")
    print(f"\n  {'k':>6}  {'recall@k':>9}  {'precision@k':>12}  {'gold in top k':>14}")
    for k, row in r["at_k"].items():
        print(f"  {k:6d}  {row['recall']:9.3f}  {row['precision']:12.4f}"
              f"  {row['hits']:14d}")

    print(f"\n-- sources {'-' * 62}")
    print(f"  planned queries      {s['planned_queries']}")
    print(f"  issued queries       {s['issued_queries']}  "
          f"(widening x{s['widening_factor']})")
    print(f"  source-queries       {s['source_queries']}")
    print(f"  papers by source     {s['papers_by_source']}")
    if any(s["errors_by_source"].values()):
        print(f"  ERRORS by source     {s['errors_by_source']}")

    e, v, w, loop = q["extraction"], q["verification"], q["writing"], q["loop"]
    print(f"\n-- extraction {'-' * 59}")
    print(f"  papers extracted     {e['papers']}")
    print(f"  mean fields of 8     {e['mean_fields_of_8']}")
    print(f"  repairs / failures   {e['repair_passes']} / {e['failed_after_repairs']}")
    print(f"  placeholder echoes   {e['placeholder_echoes_removed']}")

    print(f"\n-- writing and verification {'-' * 45}")
    print(f"  sections / refs      {w['sections']} / {w['references']}  "
          f"({w['chars']} chars, {w['citations_dropped']} citations dropped)")
    print(f"  claims               {v['claims']}")
    print(f"  supported            {v['supported']}")
    print(f"  partial              {v['partial']}")
    print(f"  dropped UNSUPPORTED  {v['unsupported_dropped']}")
    print(f"  contradicted         {v['contradicted']}")
    print(f"  abstract-only capped {v['abstract_only_capped']}")
    if v["grounding_score"] is not None:
        print(f"  GROUNDING SCORE      {v['grounding_score']:.4f}")
    if v["grounding_precision"] is not None:
        print(f"  grounding precision  {v['grounding_precision']:.4f}"
              f"   (kept claims / written claims)")
    if v["strict_precision"] is not None:
        print(f"  strict precision     {v['strict_precision']:.4f}"
              f"   (SUPPORTED only - 0 while every paper is abstract-only)")

    print(f"\n-- loop and cost {'-' * 56}")
    print(f"  critic decisions     {loop['critic_decisions']}  "
          f"(replans {loop['replans']})")
    print(f"  llm requests         {c['llm_requests']}")
    print(f"  tokens (est)         {c['total_tokens_est']:,} used, "
          f"{c['reserved_tokens_est']:,} reserved against a 200,000/day budget")
    print(f"  wall clock           {c['wall_seconds']:.0f}s "
          f"({c['wall_seconds']/60:.1f} min)")
    print(f"  by agent             {c['seconds_by_agent']}")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="T-410 - full metrics for one run.")
    ap.add_argument("--run", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--compare", help="baseline run to show deltas against")
    ap.add_argument("--runs-dir", type=pathlib.Path, default=pathlib.Path("outputs/runs"))
    ap.add_argument("--cache-dir", type=pathlib.Path,
                    default=pathlib.Path("data/llm_cache"))
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=pathlib.Path)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    metrics = collect(args.run, args.runs_dir, args.cache_dir)
    base = (collect(args.compare, args.runs_dir, args.cache_dir)
            if args.compare else None)
    render(metrics, base)

    out = args.out or pathlib.Path(f"eval/run_metrics_{args.run}.json")
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    payload = {"metrics": metrics}
    if base:
        payload["baseline"] = base
    out.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"\nwrote {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    if not corpus_path.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"{corpus_path} missing - did the run finish?")
    corpus = json.loads(corpus_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    rows = []
    if trace_path.exists():
        for line in trace_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
            try:
                rows.append(json.loads(line))
            except Exception:
                pass
    return corpus, rows


def last_payload(rows: list[dict], event: str) -> dict:
    for row in reversed(rows):
        if row.get("event") == event:
            return row.get("payload") or {}
    return {}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# metrics
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def retrieval_metrics(corpus: dict) -> dict[str, Any]:
    by_doi, by_title = load_gold()
    n_gold = len(by_doi)
    papers = corpus["papers"]
    extracted = set(corpus.get("extracted_paper_ids") or [])

    # rank position (1-indexed) of every gold paper, first occurrence wins
    ranks: dict[str, int] = {}
    in_corpus: set[str] = set()
    for i, record in enumerate(papers, 1):
        gold_doi = match(record, by_doi, by_title)
        if not gold_doi:
            continue
        ranks.setdefault(gold_doi, i)
        if record.get("paper_id") in extracted:
            in_corpus.add(gold_doi)

    at_k = {}
    for k in AT_K:
        if k > len(papers):
            continue
        hits = sum(1 for r in ranks.values() if r <= k)
        at_k[k] = {"hits": hits, "recall": hits / n_gold, "precision": hits / k}

    mrr = sum(1 / r for r in ranks.values()) / n_gold if ranks else 0.0
    return {
        "gold_papers": n_gold,
        "pool_size": len(papers),
        "corpus_size": len(extracted),
        "union_recall": len(ranks) / n_gold,
        "corpus_recall": len(in_corpus) / n_gold,
        "mrr": mrr,
        "best_rank": min(ranks.values()) if ranks else None,
        "median_rank": sorted(ranks.values())[len(ranks) // 2] if ranks else None,
        "at_k": at_k,
        "gold_ranks": dict(sorted(ranks.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1])),
        "missed": sorted(set(by_doi) - set(ranks)),
    }


def source_metrics(corpus: dict, rows: list[dict]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    log = corpus.get("retrieval_log") or []
    by_source = collections.Counter()
    returned = collections.Counter()
    errors = collections.Counter()
    for entry in log:
        by_source[entry["source"]] += entry.get("new") or 0
        returned[entry["source"]] += entry.get("returned") or 0
        if entry.get("error"):
            errors[entry["source"]] += 1
    planned = {e.get("planned_query", e.get("query")) for e in log}
    issued = {e["query"] for e in log}
    return {
        "planned_queries": len(planned),
        "issued_queries": len(issued),
        "widening_factor": round(len(issued) / len(planned), 2) if planned else None,
        "source_queries": len(log),
        "new_papers_by_source": dict(by_source),
        "returned_by_source": dict(returned),
        "errors_by_source": dict(errors),
        "papers_by_source": dict(collections.Counter(
            p.get("source") for p in corpus["papers"])),
    }


def quality_metrics(rows: list[dict]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    extract = last_payload(rows, "extract_summary")
    verify = last_payload(rows, "verification_summary")
    review = last_payload(rows, "review_written")
    decisions = [r["payload"].get("decision") for r in rows
                 if r.get("event") == "critic_decision"]
    claims = verify.get("claims") or 0
    supported = verify.get("supported") or 0
    partial = verify.get("partial") or 0
    dropped = verify.get("dropped") or 0
    return {
        "extraction": {
            "papers": extract.get("papers"),
            "mean_fields_of_8": extract.get("mean_fields_of_8"),
            "repair_passes": extract.get("repair_passes"),
            "failed_after_repairs": extract.get("failed_after_repairs"),
            "placeholder_echoes_removed": extract.get("placeholder_echoes_removed"),
            "skipped_no_text": extract.get("skipped_no_text"),
        },
        "writing": {
            "sections": review.get("sections"),
            "references": review.get("references"),
            "chars": review.get("chars"),
            "citations_dropped": review.get("citations_dropped"),
        },
        "verification": {
            "claims": claims,
            "supported": supported,
            "partial": partial,
            "unsupported_dropped": dropped,
            "contradicted": verify.get("contradicted"),
            "abstract_only_capped": verify.get("abstract_only_capped"),
            "grounding_score": verify.get("grounding_score"),
            # The headline quality number: of the claims written, the share the
            # Verifier could stand behind at all (SUPPORTED or PARTIAL).
            "grounding_precision": (claims - dropped) / claims if claims else None,
            # And the strict one: full support, not partial.
            "strict_precision": supported / claims if claims else None,
        },
        "loop": {
            "critic_decisions": decisions,
            "iterations": max((r.get("iteration") or 0) for r in rows) if rows else 0,
            "replans": sum(1 for d in decisions if d == "REPLAN"),
        },
    }


def cost_metrics(rows: list[dict], cache_dir: pathlib.Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    from researchgpt.core.llm import estimate_tokens

    requests = [r for r in rows if r.get("event") == "request"]
    prompt_tokens = response_tokens = 0
    for req in requests:
        digest = (req.get("payload") or {}).get("prompt_hash")
        path = cache_dir / f"{digest}.json"
        if not path.exists():
            continue
        entry = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        prompt_tokens += estimate_tokens(entry.get("prompt") or "")
        response_tokens += estimate_tokens(entry.get("response") or "")

    per_agent: dict[str, float] = {}
    started: dict[str, datetime] = {}
    for row in rows:
        when = datetime.fromisoformat(row["ts"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        if row.get("event") == "agent_start":
            started[row["agent"]] = when
        elif row.get("event") == "agent_end" and row["agent"] in started:
            per_agent[row["agent"]] = round(
                per_agent.get(row["agent"], 0.0)
                + (when - started[row["agent"]]).total_seconds(), 1)
    wall = 0.0
    if rows:
        wall = (datetime.fromisoformat(rows[-1]["ts"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
                - datetime.fromisoformat(rows[0]["ts"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
                ).total_seconds()
    return {
        "llm_requests": len(requests),
        "prompt_tokens_est": prompt_tokens,
        "response_tokens_est": response_tokens,
        "total_tokens_est": prompt_tokens + response_tokens,
        # What the provider actually reserves per request at admission, which is
        # the number that exhausts a daily budget (measured from a Groq 429:
        # "Requested 5520" = a 3,472-token prompt + max_tokens 2048).
        "reserved_tokens_est": prompt_tokens + 2048 * len(requests),
        "wall_seconds": round(wall, 1),
        "seconds_by_agent": per_agent,
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# report
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def collect(run: str, runs_dir: pathlib.Path, cache_dir: pathlib.Path) -> dict[str, Any]:
    corpus, rows = load_run(runs_dir / run)
    return {
        "run": run,
        "retrieval": retrieval_metrics(corpus),
        "sources": source_metrics(corpus, rows),
        "quality": quality_metrics(rows),
        "cost": cost_metrics(rows, cache_dir),
        "ranking_order_verified": bool(
            last_payload(rows, "rank_summary")), # a rank_summary means the
        # Ranker ran; without it corpus.json is insertion order and every @k
        # below is meaningless (the T-212 defect).
    }


def render(m: dict[str, Any], base: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> None:
    r, s, q, c = m["retrieval"], m["sources"], m["quality"], m["cost"]

    def delta(new, old, fmt="{:+.3f}"):
        if base is None or old is None or new is None:
            return ""
        return "   " + fmt.format(new - old)

    br = base["retrieval"] if base else None
    print(f"\n{'=' * 74}\nRUN METRICS - {m['run']}\n{'=' * 74}")
    if base:
        print(f"(deltas against {base['run']})")
    if not m["ranking_order_verified"]:
        print("\n  !! no rank_summary in the trace - corpus.json is INSERTION "
              "order, so every @k number below is meaningless")

    print(f"\n-- retrieval, against a {r['gold_papers']}-paper answer key "
          f"{'-' * 22}")
    print(f"  pool size            {r['pool_size']:6d}"
          + (f"   ({base['retrieval']['pool_size']} before)" if base else ""))
    print(f"  UNION RECALL         {r['union_recall']:6.3f}   "
          f"({len(r['gold_ranks'])}/{r['gold_papers']})"
          + delta(r["union_recall"], br and br["union_recall"]))
    print(f"  corpus recall        {r['corpus_recall']:6.3f}   "
          f"(bounded by max_papers/{r['gold_papers']})"
          + delta(r["corpus_recall"], br and br["corpus_recall"]))
    print(f"  MRR                  {r['mrr']:6.3f}"
          + delta(r["mrr"], br and br["mrr"]))
    print(f"  best / median rank   {r['best_rank']} / {r['median_rank']}")
    print(f"\n  {'k':>6}  {'recall@k':>9}  {'precision@k':>12}  {'gold in top k':>14}")
    for k, row in r["at_k"].items():
        print(f"  {k:6d}  {row['recall']:9.3f}  {row['precision']:12.4f}"
              f"  {row['hits']:14d}")

    print(f"\n-- sources {'-' * 62}")
    print(f"  planned queries      {s['planned_queries']}")
    print(f"  issued queries       {s['issued_queries']}  "
          f"(widening x{s['widening_factor']})")
    print(f"  source-queries       {s['source_queries']}")
    print(f"  papers by source     {s['papers_by_source']}")
    if any(s["errors_by_source"].values()):
        print(f"  ERRORS by source     {s['errors_by_source']}")

    e, v, w, loop = q["extraction"], q["verification"], q["writing"], q["loop"]
    print(f"\n-- extraction {'-' * 59}")
    print(f"  papers extracted     {e['papers']}")
    print(f"  mean fields of 8     {e['mean_fields_of_8']}")
    print(f"  repairs / failures   {e['repair_passes']} / {e['failed_after_repairs']}")
    print(f"  placeholder echoes   {e['placeholder_echoes_removed']}")

    print(f"\n-- writing and verification {'-' * 45}")
    print(f"  sections / refs      {w['sections']} / {w['references']}  "
          f"({w['chars']} chars, {w['citations_dropped']} citations dropped)")
    print(f"  claims               {v['claims']}")
    print(f"  supported            {v['supported']}")
    print(f"  partial              {v['partial']}")
    print(f"  dropped UNSUPPORTED  {v['unsupported_dropped']}")
    print(f"  contradicted         {v['contradicted']}")
    print(f"  abstract-only capped {v['abstract_only_capped']}")
    if v["grounding_score"] is not None:
        print(f"  GROUNDING SCORE      {v['grounding_score']:.4f}")
    if v["grounding_precision"] is not None:
        print(f"  grounding precision  {v['grounding_precision']:.4f}"
              f"   (kept claims / written claims)")
    if v["strict_precision"] is not None:
        print(f"  strict precision     {v['strict_precision']:.4f}"
              f"   (SUPPORTED only - 0 while every paper is abstract-only)")

    print(f"\n-- loop and cost {'-' * 56}")
    print(f"  critic decisions     {loop['critic_decisions']}  "
          f"(replans {loop['replans']})")
    print(f"  llm requests         {c['llm_requests']}")
    print(f"  tokens (est)         {c['total_tokens_est']:,} used, "
          f"{c['reserved_tokens_est']:,} reserved against a 200,000/day budget")
    print(f"  wall clock           {c['wall_seconds']:.0f}s "
          f"({c['wall_seconds']/60:.1f} min)")
    print(f"  by agent             {c['seconds_by_agent']}")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="T-410 - full metrics for one run.")
    ap.add_argument("--run", required=True)
    ap.add_argument("--compare", help="baseline run to show deltas against")
    ap.add_argument("--runs-dir", type=pathlib.Path, default=pathlib.Path("outputs/runs"))
    ap.add_argument("--cache-dir", type=pathlib.Path,
                    default=pathlib.Path("data/llm_cache"))
    ap.add_argument("--out", type=pathlib.Path)
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    metrics = collect(args.run, args.runs_dir, args.cache_dir)
    base = (collect(args.compare, args.runs_dir, args.cache_dir)
            if args.compare else None)
    render(metrics, base)

    out = args.out or pathlib.Path(f"eval/run_metrics_{args.run}.json")
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    payload = {"metrics": metrics}
    if base:
        payload["baseline"] = base
    out.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"\nwrote {out}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
